title: Trees thin toward a river, driftwood on its bank

checks.description: The river output is one or more open polylines (none ends at its own first point, by index or within 2 m) that, inside the ground's bounding rectangle, span at least 80% of its width or depth.
At least 100 trees; over ground within 10 m of some tree, the tree density 2-12 m from the river polyline is between 10% and 60% of the density more than 30 m from it.
Trees 2-12 m from the river polyline average at most 70% of the size (mean instance scale) of trees more than 30 m from it.
No tree stands within 2 m of the river polyline (the water).
At least 99% of trees have their base within 0.5 m of the ground under them (the ground mesh, or the nearest ground point when it has no triangles).
At least 10 pieces of driftwood, and at least 90% of them lie 2-8 m from the river polyline with their origin within 0.5 m of the ground under them.

The river's parts with ground within 4 m of them (the ground mesh, or its bounding rectangle when it has no triangles), joined in order, cut into 10 equal stretches: driftwood within 25 m of those parts, each assigned to its nearest stretch, reaches at least 8 of them.
